verdict.rationale: Installed plugins and skills are driven through natural-language chat in ChatGPT and Codex. Codex loads a skill's full instructions when it decides the skill is relevant (docs-49), and plugins act on conversational requests such as summarizing Slack channels or drafting replies (docs-4) and sending messages on your behalf (docs-5). Authoring is also conversational: the creator asks what a skill should do (docs-7), the recorder drafts a skill from a demonstration (docs-16), and a community user confirms explicit natural-language invocation like "use the PR skill to open a PR" (comm-8). missing for 10: plugin installation and management are shown only through slash or `$` commands and UI tabs (/plugins, `$skill-installer`, the Plugins tab) rather than free-form language, and there are no independent hands-on reports on how reliably natural-language commands work.
